note: No imported register; Greek gazette (FEK) list on el.wikipedia has no Corfu row. Island yields two serious olives; page needs four.

leads.name: Evdokia olive, Strogili (Strongyli), South Corfu
leads.reason: Real and well covered (TU Dresden, Prof. Andrea Roloff, roots dated ~1086 to 1200 years, planted around 928 AD; iefimerida, himara.gr, Greek Reporter; schools and tourists visit; a few metres from the former home of poet Gerasimos Markoras per enimerosi.com). Held: no girth, no tree coordinate, no photo in reach; only village level (Strogili 39.5168, 19.9239, Melitieis, South Corfu; not the hamlet of the same name in the north). Landowner allows visits via the Union of Ionian Islanders. No official designation yet (union seeks monumental olive status). Needs a pin or Commons photo.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

leads.name: Age-old elm, Kassiopi
leads.reason: Public space, pre-1864 planting per the Corfu Society for the Protection of the Environment (enimerosi.com, 2019 appeal not to cut it). No pin, may since have been felled; unverified alive.

leads.name: Pedunculate oak beside the Heraion, Mon Repos (registry 102)
leads.reason: Greek Tree Registry entry 102: girth 3.74 m, height 21.67 m, 39.603757, 19.924831, beside the archaic Temple of Hera in Mon Repos; the park holds several of this rare subspecies, some possibly native. Registry text marks it only as a representative of the rare subspecies, not as a standout beyond size; no recording date. Held as a lead, not a destination of its own. Registry (c) Friends of the National Parks: facts only.
